subject: Clarify CCPA/CPRA addendum: transit encryption, subprocessor onboarding & onshore fallback
messages:
From: Suresh Rao <suresh@brightgate.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@brightgate.com
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: CCPA/CPRA addendum — brightgate redlines and a couple clarifications

Marissa,

Thanks for sending the draft US privacy addendum last week. Our legal team reviewed and surfaced two items we need clarified before we can move to procurement:

- Encryption in transit: we want explicit language that all customer data moved between Brightgate and Redwood (including internal cache replication) is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2+ and that any third-party transfer channels meet the same standard.
- Subprocessor onboarding: Brightgate requires a 10-business-day notice and a documented onshore fallback plan for subprocessors that handle US personal data (we need to understand Redwood's timeline and evidence).

I've attached our redlines for the doc (brightgate_ccpa_redlines_v1.pdf). Can you let us know whether Redwood can accept the notice window and the encryption wording? If not, what alternative language would you propose?

Appreciate a quick turn — our procurement deadline is the week of June 7.

Best,
Suresh Rao
Head of Legal Operations
Brightgate Systems
[Attachment: brightgate_ccpa_redlines_v1.pdf]

From: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Suresh Rao <suresh@brightgate.com>
Cc: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum — brightgate redlines and a couple clarifications

Suresh — thanks for the redlines, and for flagging procurement timing. Looping in Aditya (product/privacy lead) and Karthik (security/legal interface) to confirm.

Quick note on the two asks:
- TLS / encryption in transit: Redwood enforces TLS1.2+ for all public endpoints and mTLS for inter-datacenter service-to-service replication in hosted and dedicated modes. We can accept explicit language that traffic is encrypted in transit and will update the addendum text to reference TLS1.2+ (or newer) and require equivalent protections for any third-party transfer channel.
- Subprocessor notice & onshore fallback: our standard is 15-calendar-day notice for planned subprocessor additions, with an emergency onboarding process for incidents. We can make an exception to provide a 10-business-day notice for Brightgate (we'll document it in the addendum), but we need to clarify what Brightgate considers an acceptable "onshore fallback" (e.g., transfer halt + onshore repointing, or additional onshore subprocessors).

I've attached a short excerpt with suggested language for the service-provider clause and the transit encryption line. If that looks OK I can circulate a redline back to your legal team.

Thanks — will follow up after Aditya/Karthik weigh in.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Director, Privacy & Policy
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_dpa_sp_clauses_v1.docx]

From: aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 08:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum — brightgate redlines and a couple clarifications

Marissa / Karthik — tagging in a couple of practical constraints so the reply to Brightgate is operationally accurate:

1) Encryption: agree with calling out TLS1.2+ for external endpoints. For certain internal pipelines (e.g., GPU node KV cache replication) we rely on private networking + mTLS; we can state "encrypted in transit (TLS1.2+ or equivalent including mTLS for internal channels)".

2) Notice period: 10-business-day notice for non-emergency subprocessors is acceptable for this account. For emergency subprocessors (incident response or critical capacity), we should keep the existing emergency onboarding language with post-facto notice and evidence.

3) Onshore fallback: we need to define the SLA/Burst model. Proposal: Redwood will maintain (a) an onshore fallback plan documented in the addendum describing options (onshore repointing, capacity pre-provisioning or data routing isolation) and (b) an operational playbook available under NDA with timelines for activation. We should avoid committing to a hard-time SLA on provisioning new onshore subprocessors unless the customer buys dedicated capacity.

If Brightgate insists on hard provisioning SLAs for onshore takeover, we should price that as an add-on.

I'll add two short bullets to Marissa's doc and send back to Suresh.

- Aditya
Product & Privacy
Redwood Inference

From: Suresh Rao <suresh@brightgate.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: legal@brightgate.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2026 12:54:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum — brightgate redlines and a couple clarifications

Marissa / Aditya — thanks for the quick follow. A few clarifications from our side after reviewing your notes:

- The proposed encryption language looks fine. Please include the explicit phrase "TLS 1.2 or higher, or equivalent cryptographic protection (including mTLS) for internal service channels" in the addendum.
- On subprocessors: Brightgate's procurement team requires a 10-business-day notice for planned additions (non-emergency) and a documented fallback plan that states our options in the event of an offshore subprocessors incapacity. We understand you won't commit to provisioning SLAs without dedicated capacity; acceptable — we just need the plan documented and an escalation path with named contacts.

I've attached our annotated redlines reflecting the above and a DocuSign envelope for the DPA (we'll hold signature until we see Redwood's updated redline).

Best,
Suresh
[Attachment: brightgate_ccpa_redlines_v1.pdf]

From: karthik_iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 30 May 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: CCPA/CPRA addendum — brightgate redlines and a couple clarifications

Team — finalizing the response to Brightgate. Draft items to include in our redline reply: 

1) Encryption line: "Provider will ensure all Customer Personal Data is encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher or an equivalent cryptographic protocol (including mutual TLS) for inter-service/internal channels)."

2) Subprocessor notice: "Provider agrees to provide Customer with at least ten (10) business days' prior notice of any planned additions of subprocessors that will process Customer Personal Data in the United States. For emergency subprocessors, Provider shall provide prompt notice and a post-event report detailing the reasons for emergency onboarding and measures taken."

3) Onshore fallback: include an "Onshore Fallback Playbook" as an appendix available under NDA that documents: named escalation contacts, options (repointing, data routing isolation, temporary onshore capacity via cloud marketplace partners), and target activation timelines for documented scenarios. Note: reserve any provisioning SLA commitments for customers who purchase dedicated capacity.

4) Evidence/SOC2: offer SOC 2 Type II report access via secure upload link and allow a short attestation letter for telemetry/dataflow mapping.

If everyone approves, I'll incorporate and send the updated redline to Suresh with the attachments and the DocuSign link note. Also propose a 30-minute sync tomorrow to align procurement and SRE on the playbook.

— Karthik
Security & Compliance Interface
Redwood Inference
